scenes.headline: How Sana makes high-resolution diffusion cheap
scenes.sub: NVIDIA's Sana: a deep-compression autoencoder and a linear-attention transformer.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Tortilla! Sana is known as the linear-attention image model. But its bigger trick happens before attention even runs. Here's how it works.

scenes.text: Sana's autoencoder compresses 32 times per side with patch size 1, so the transformer sees four times fewer tokens before any attention runs.
scenes.say: Sana's autoencoder compresses thirty-two times per side, with patch size one. So the transformer sees four times fewer tokens, before any attention runs.

steps.say: A diffusion transformer works on an autoencoder's latents. FLUX and SD3 shrink each side eight times, then patch by two: a 1024 pixel image becomes 4096 tokens.
Sana's autoencoder shrinks each side thirty-two times, with no patching on top. The same image is a thirty-two by thirty-two grid: 1024 tokens.
The transformer denoises that grid. Its self-attention is linear, so cost grows with the token count, not its square.
The prompt goes through Gemma, a small language model with its head removed. The transformer reads it through ordinary softmax cross-attention.

scenes.title: What linear attention computes
scenes.say: Softmax attention builds a token-by-token matrix. Swap the exponential for a ReLU, and you can multiply in a different order.

parts.note: keys times values first: a 32 x 32 state
parts.say: Keys times values first. That's a small thirty-two by thirty-two state, the same size at every resolution.

parts.note: each query reads the state: linear in tokens
parts.say: Then each query reads that state, so the cost is linear in the number of tokens.

scenes.title: What each lever buys, given the other
scenes.say: Given the autoencoder, linear attention buys one point one two times at ten twenty-four pixels, and three at forty ninety-six. The autoencoder always buys about four.

scenes.text: At every resolution Sana ships, the autoencoder is the bigger lever. Linear attention is insurance against the resolution going up.
scenes.mark: the autoencoder is the bigger lever

recap: A 32x autoencoder: four times fewer tokens
Linear attention keeps a fixed-size state
scenes.say: To recap: compress harder before the transformer, keep attention's state small, and know where each lever pays.
